facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.site: Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility
facts.title: unplanned release of chemical energy at TK-4211

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control BLAST_GUARDING_AND_CLEARANCE: the guarding, clearance and misfire handling for a blast was in place but did not perform, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next field verification that the guarding, clearance and misfire handling for a blast on TK-4211 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in charging and firing, specifically charging, tying in and guarding a blast. TK-4211 (hydrocarbon day tanks and surge vessel) is in service for diesel and light hydrocarbon day storage, discharge surge suppression. The task proceeded during start-up after maintenance while the guarding, clearance and misfire handling for a blast was in place but did not perform. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 26 September 2013 a hazard report was recorded on TK-4211 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during start-up after maintenance; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
